### Risks

- No old hash replacement, diagnostic deletion or unsupported assertion that the historic observation was false.

### Acceptance criteria

- The review retains original bytes, IDs, receipt/hash provenance and the two changed artifact paths.
- Accessible immutable proof, missing historical proof and present applicability are distinguished; a justified disposition is reviewable before any root record mutation.

### Planned verification

- Reopen exact cited sources and compare recorded versus current versions without updating them.
- Determine whether a current claim needs fresh verification or a historical-only/superseded/retracted treatment; retain the reason and operation scope.

## TASK-010 - Implement historical support and applicability distinctions

Extend the owning memory evidence contract and diagnostics to separate integrity of retained historical proof from applicability to live versions, with a backward-compatible treatment for existing records.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Status | `planned` |
| State reason | None |
| Skip authority | None |
| Requirements | REQ-008, REQ-013, REQ-014 |
| Design basis | None |
| Target artifacts | SKILLS-depo/memory/scripts/memory_evidence.py, SKILLS-depo/memory/references/evidence-and-lifecycle.md, MEMORY-depo/publication-and-recovery.md, Verification/ontology-health-repairs/memory/evidence-design.md |
| Dependencies | TASK-002, TASK-009 |
| Parallel group | None |
| Completed at | None |

### Risks

- A digest without accessible proof cannot establish a historical observation; broader schema changes require a specific design decision.

### Acceptance criteria

- Exact accessible historical evidence can remain historically supported while later implementation versions mark current applicability stale/changed/unverified.
- Missing/altered evidence stays diagnosed and cannot enter trusted current-authority or verified-current results; nested diagnostics identify the changed artifact and safe expected/current versions.
- The chosen durable evidence representation uses existing governed paths, privacy/resource bounds and explicit compatibility handling, without implicitly migrating memory-record or Task schemas.

### Planned verification

- Review the schema/reader/publication compatibility against current records and caller behavior.
- Exercise intact archived evidence, changed live code, absent archived bytes and tampered evidence controls.

### Risks

- Tests must never fabricate a success receipt for the real historical record.

### Acceptance criteria

- A controlled later source update preserves reproducibility of the earlier observation while invalidating unsupported current applicability.
- New claims require actual observed verification and permitted retained bytes; supersession/retraction preserve prior provenance and exact version checks.
- Current authorization and trust filters reject unsupported evidence; the real-root record disposition is reserved for TASK-028.

### Planned verification

- Run focused publication, capture, evidence and recovery tests with compatible legacy and new evidence.
- Reopen generated fixture receipts/records and test both historical retrieval and exclusion from verified-current authority.
